body:
m1 - DO NOT GATE THE STACK YET. My 4383a85 BREAKS codecJVM. I found it myself, I am fixing it now, and I will post a corrected SHA. Details so you can judge rather than take my word.

WHAT BROKE: CodecGens.recall builds a RecallGraph whose two units have text that does not match their spans. Transcript is "A woman went home. Then she slept."; the sentence spans include the terminal period, the unit text omits it - "A woman went home" against a span covering "A woman went home.". My new law refuses exactly that, so the fixture object fails construction and takes the whole codec module down with an ExceptionInInitializerError.

MY PROCESS FAILURE, plainly: my gate for 4383a85 ran recall on three platforms, align, fixtures, interview and laws. IT DID NOT RUN CODEC. I added a validation law to a core type used by six modules and gated the five I happened to think of. That is the same shape as the mutation that survived because the fixture could not reach the branch - I checked the places I imagined, not the places that exist. The rule I should have applied: a change to a VALIDATION LAW on a shared type is gated by compileAll plus every module that constructs that type, not by the modules I was thinking about.

WHY I AM NOT WEAKENING THE LAW, though that would be the fast fix. The real segmenter produces unit text INCLUDING terminal punctuation - that is why recall's own GraphSuite, AnnaFixture and the WOG fixtures all pass unchanged. The codec fixture is hand-written and is precisely the incoherent object the law exists to forbid: a unit whose text is not the words at its span. Trimming punctuation in the comparison, or dropping the law, would make the fixture legal by making the guarantee meaningless, and this is the case that proves the guarantee bites. So I am fixing the FIXTURE.

ONE CONSEQUENCE YOU SHOULD KNOW ABOUT BEFORE I DO IT: AlignWire.recallChecksum hashes unit text, so correcting the fixture text CHANGES the recall checksum and therefore the encoded JSON in AlignCodecSuite's round-trip assertions. I will report exactly what moved and why, the same way I did for the WOG golden, rather than quietly re-cutting expectations. If any of that turns out to touch an artifact you would rather rule on first, say so and I will stop.

CodecGens.scala is unreserved; cursor-grok-storymodel4s holds only sidecar.scala, SidecarSuite.scala and ConstructionProbeSuite.scala, none of which I need. I will reserve before editing.

The other six commits in the stack are unaffected - the breakage is specific to the recall validation law.
